title: The ticket table
prompt:
`b02_tickets.csv` holds twelve fictional tickets. Finish `load(path)` so it reads the file with pandas and returns `X`, a DataFrame with the `hours` and `parts` columns, and `y`, the `cost` column as a Series.

Run it inside your virtual environment. `python3 table.py` prints the two shapes.
hints: `pd.read_csv(path, encoding="utf-8")` gives you the whole table as a DataFrame. Call it `df`.
A list of column names in square brackets picks several columns: `df[["hours", "parts"]]`. One name picks one column as a Series: `df["cost"]`.
Three lines: `df = pd.read_csv(path, encoding="utf-8")`, `X = df[["hours", "parts"]]`, `y = df["cost"]`, then `return X, y`.
explain_after: A DataFrame is a two-dimensional table whose columns can hold different types, and a Series is one column [ml-024]. The shape `(12, 2)` is the form scikit-learn expects for `X`: one row per sample and one column per feature [ml-026].
